# Plan: new record id with path-unsafe chars (loose pattern, e.g. `.*`) → `validation_pk_forbidden` error

Status: DRAFT

## Claims

| # | Claim | Kind | Blocks done? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| c1 | A new record's primary key is rejected if it contains a control character (any 0x00–0x1F or 0x7F, e.g. NUL, `\n`, `\t`), even when the pattern allows anything | behavior_change | Yes |
| c2 | A new record's primary key is rejected if it contains any Windows-reserved character `: * ? " < > \|` | behavior_change | Yes |
| c3 | A new record's primary key is rejected if it is exactly `.` or `..`, or if it ends with `.` or a space | behavior_change | Yes |
| c4 | These ids are still accepted with a loose pattern: `abc`, `a.b`, `a-b_c`, `a b`, `.abc`, unicode `ид123` | no_behavior_change | Yes |
| c5 | `/` and `\` are still rejected in primary keys. None of the new characters are rejected in non-primary-key text fields. Records already saved with such ids still pass validation on update | no_behavior_change | Yes |

## Checks

| Claim | Type | Check | New? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| c1–c3 | Unit | New table cases in `TestTextFieldValidateValue` (`core/field_text_test.go`): primary-key field with `Pattern: ".*"`, one case per bad id, expect an error | New |
| c4 | Unit | Same table: the valid ids above, primary-key field with `Pattern: ".*"`, expect no error | New |
| c5 | Unit | The existing `/`, `\` and non-primary-key cases still pass. New non-primary-key cases for `:`, `..` and NUL expect no error. New case: a saved record with id `a:b` is updated and expects no error | Existing + New |

Regression scope: `go test ./core -run TestTextField` · baseline: 76 passed, 0 failed
Skipped: integration/API tests, because the API create path goes through the same `TextField.ValidateValue` check. Filesystem tests, because nothing in the filesystem code changes.

Approve, or edit?

Reject `.` and space anywhere in the id, so `a.b`, `a b` and `.abc` must fail. Also reject `' \` % $`. For control characters, only NUL, tab, newline and carriage return.
Also reject ids that exactly match CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1–COM9 or LPT1–LPT9 in any case. Something like `console` is still fine.
The error should be on the id field and name the offending character.
Approved for the rest.

I've added your edits: new record ids are now rejected if they contain one of the forbidden characters (including `.` and space anywhere) or exactly match a Windows device name. All six claims pass, and the regression scope has 85 passing (76 baseline plus 9 new), with no failures.

The error is on the `id` field and names the offending character in quotes, so a NUL shows as `"\x00"`, or the reserved name, like `"com3"`. Ids already saved are not re-checked when the record is updated.

The fix is in `core/field_text.go`; nothing is committed. Details are in `.verify/report.md`.
